channel.title: North Seattle Dispatch
channel.description: North Seattle news, once a week, from the North Seattle Dispatch.

item.title: The I-5 southbound on-ramp at NE 130th Street did not reopen for good on November 5: it is closed again until as soon as 5 AM Friday, November 13
item.description: SDOT's November 6 update opened the ramp for the weekend from as soon as 5 PM Friday, November 6, and restarted the around-the-clock closure as soon as 5 AM Monday, November 9.

item.title: The council's committee votes on the 2027 budget start Friday, November 13, at 9:30 AM, and the final vote is set for Friday, November 20, at 1 PM
item.description: After last Thursday's public hearing, the council's calendar set this week aside for amendments, with more committee votes on November 16 and 19.

item.title: The city has posted a draft vision for the North Aurora corridor, N 80th to N 145th Streets, and is taking comments on it online
item.description: The North Aurora Community Action Plan runs past Bitter Lake and Haller Lake and will set short- and long-term strategies for the corridor's streets and growth, plus early actions for the next one to two years.

item.title: free extra leaf pickup, all November
item.description: Through November, Seattle Public Utilities takes up to 10 extra bags of leaves free on each collection day for household food and yard waste customers.

item.title: About the history of Roosevelt north of NE 130th Street, and how I-5 changed it
item.description: A reader asked about the history of Roosevelt north of NE 130th Street, and how I-5 changed it.

item.title: The I-5 southbound on-ramp at NE 130th Street is due to reopen at 5 AM Thursday, November 5
item.description: SDOT's last posted update, dated October 23, schedules the reopening for then and says the dates can change.

item.title: The city's budget calendar lists the balancing package as published November 3, with a Budget Chair briefing and a public hearing this week
item.description: The calendar puts the proposed balancing package before the budget committee Wednesday at 9:30 AM. The public hearing is Thursday, November 5: remote comment starts at 1 PM and in-person comment at 5 PM. The calendar says the schedule is subject to change.

item.title: a shutoff valve you can find before the freeze
item.description: Know where your main water shutoff is, usually in a basement, crawlspace or garage, indoors or out, before you need it.

item.title: When the big Japanese grocery on Aurora opens
item.description: A reader asked when the big Japanese grocery on Aurora opens.

item.title: The I-5 southbound on-ramp at NE 130th Street is now scheduled to stay closed until 5 AM Thursday, November 5
item.description: SDOT's schedule has it closed around the clock from 5 AM Monday, October 26, for demolition and concrete work.

item.title: Ballots for the November 3 general election are due by 8 PM Tuesday
item.description: King County's 100 drop boxes close at 8 PM sharp on Election Day, and a mailed ballot must be postmarked by Election Day to count.

item.title: Tonight and Friday night, from 11 PM, light rail runs on one track at Pinehurst and Shoreline South/148th
item.description: Expect delays of up to 20 minutes toward Lynnwood City Center, and 2 Line trains turn back at Northgate.

item.title: The council's budget package comes out Tuesday, November 3, and the public hearing is Thursday, November 5
item.description: The budget committee takes the package up Wednesday at 9:30 AM. At the hearing, remote comment starts at 1 PM and in-person comment at 5 PM; written comment to councilmembers is open any time.

item.title: You can ask for a public EV charger at the curb near where you live
item.description: Seattle City Light and SDOT are adding up to 200 curbside charging locations; applications stay open through fall 2027, and installation runs from fall 2027 through 2030.

item.title: new batteries when the clocks change
item.description: Clocks fall back one hour at 2 AM Sunday, November 1.

item.title: How to reach Golden Gardens Park by bus, and what the walk is like
item.description: A reader asked how to reach Golden Gardens Park by bus, and what the walk is like.

item.title: The I-5 southbound on-ramp at NE 130th Street now closes as soon as Monday, October 26, a week later than first scheduled
item.description: The closure is around the clock for about 14 days of demolition and concrete work.

item.title: The new roundabout at Roosevelt Way NE and 10th Ave NE is open to vehicles in all directions
item.description: It has flashing crossing beacons and curb-protected bike lanes; SDOT's project page shows how to walk, bike and drive through it.

item.title: Several elevators at Pinehurst Station have been out since Monday, October 19
item.description: For the Lynnwood platform, go to the south end of the plaza and take elevator 1; for the Federal Way and Downtown Redmond platform, elevator 2.

item.title: Carkeek Park's free salmon weekends start Saturday, October 24
item.description: Creekside Salmon Journey Days run Saturdays and Sundays through December 6, 10:30 AM to 3:30 PM, on Piper's Creek.

item.title: Three free Halloween events at North Seattle community centers
item.description: Northgate's family pumpkin carving is Friday, October 23, 4:30 to 6:30 PM (not Monday, as issue one had it).

item.title: clear the drain, not the street
item.description: Leaves on a storm grate back water up onto the street and toward basements once the November rain starts.

item.title: The I-5 southbound on-ramp at NE 130th Street closes around the clock for about 14 days, starting as soon as Monday, October 19
item.description: SDOT needs it for demolition and concrete work on the NE 130th and NE 125th Street project.

item.title: Pinehurst Station is open, and this weekend the 2 Line runs on buses between Downtown and the Eastside
item.description: The station opened September 30 on the west side of 5th Ave NE at NE 130th Street, with 1 and 2 Line trains every 4 to 5 minutes and Westlake 15 minutes away.

item.title: Seattle's 2027–28 budget: public hearing November 5, final vote November 20
item.description: The council publishes its balancing package November 3.

item.title: Want your block closed for Halloween? Apply by Tuesday, October 20
item.description: SDOT's Trick-or-Streets permits are free for events open to the public, between October 21 and November 2: up to three consecutive blocks, until 10 PM, with cross streets left open.

item.title: November 2, not October 31
item.description: The second half of 2026 King County property tax is due Monday, November 2.
